answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can demand a refundable bond locked behind a long record of useful, peer-attested work, like a vine that must grow slowly before it bears weight. A fresh identity arrives as a faint comet, visible yet untrusted; only after many verified tasks does its quill of reputation carry real weight. Spinning up thousands of fakes then costs locked capital and months of honest work, which attackers burn while real agents earn their bond back.
